# onpager_team_role_defaults (Resource)

Manage the tenant's complete live team member and additional lead role policy. Configure one resource per tenant. Destroy clears both sets and removes these dynamic grants tenant-wide.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Import the existing tenant policy before applying when either set is nonempty.
data "onpager_rbac_role" "member" {
  key = "team_viewer"
}

data "onpager_rbac_role" "lead" {
  key = "team_administrator"
}

resource "onpager_team_role_defaults" "example" {
  members = [data.onpager_rbac_role.member.id]
  leads   = [data.onpager_rbac_role.lead.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `leads` (Set of String) Complete set of additional team-scope role UUIDs granted live to active team leads in their teams. Leads also receive members roles. Explicit [] is valid and grants no additional lead roles; omitted/null and null elements are invalid. Unknown UUIDs are deferred until apply; UUIDs must be nonzero canonical lowercase values.
- `members` (Set of String) Complete set of team-scope role UUIDs granted live to all current and future active team members, including leads, in each member's team. Builtin or custom roles must already exist. Explicit [] is valid and grants no member roles; omitted/null and null elements are invalid. Unknown UUIDs are deferred until apply; UUIDs must be nonzero canonical lowercase values.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable singleton identity and import ID: `tenant`.
- `revision` (Number) Current positive whole-policy revision, validated against its strong numeric ETag and used in If-Match for replacement and destroy. Independent of role and assignment revisions. Stale revisions return HTTP 412; run a new plan before retrying.

## Import

Import the existing complete policy with the literal ID `tenant`, including an
empty policy. Import and refresh read only. Fresh installations normally contain
seeded member and lead roles, so import before applying this resource.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_team_role_defaults.example
  id = "tenant"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_team_role_defaults.example tenant
```

## Policy scope and ownership

Configure one resource per tenant. It owns both complete role sets for all
current and future teams. Roles apply dynamically while an active membership
exists in a team; they are not copied into direct user assignments. Team leads
receive the member set plus the additional lead set. This policy does not grant
service accounts human team membership or alter their explicit role assignments.

Both `members` and `leads` are required sets of existing team-scope role UUIDs.
Built-in and custom team roles are supported. Duplicate configured UUIDs have
set semantics; order is insignificant. Explicit `[]` selects no roles for that
category. Omitted/null sets and null elements are invalid; references may be
unknown during planning but must resolve to valid UUIDs before apply. Tenant-scope
roles and nonexistent roles are rejected by the API. No role, assignment or
roster entry is created implicitly.

Create first reads the existing policy. Any nonempty member or lead set requires
explicit import, even if the configured sets already match. The provider never
merges or silently adopts existing grants. If both the observed policy and both
configured sets are empty, create adopts the observed policy without a write and
saves its verified revision. Publishing nonempty configured sets from an empty
baseline uses that read's own revision for compare-and-swap.

## Updates and destroy

Updates atomically replace both sets using the saved whole-policy strong numeric
ETag. Role, assignment and other IAM revisions cannot substitute for it. A stale
revision returns HTTP 412 and requires a new plan. The provider does not re-read
to rebase a failed write or retry it automatically. UI display names and role
pickers are not part of configuration or refresh.

Destroy publishes `members = []` and `leads = []` using the saved policy revision.
This removes these dynamic grants from all current teams and future memberships.
It does not restore seeded or previous defaults. Direct assignments, group
assignments and other grant sources remain independent. Use credentials whose
required authority survives this change.

The API policy always exists; an empty policy remains a managed object until
destroy succeeds. Authentication, authorization, transport, malformed-response
and HTTP errors, including an unexpected GET 404, retain state. Failed writes
retain the saved state. A confirmed write with a malformed success body preserves
the requested complete sets and any independently verified committed revision;
refresh is required when a usable revision was not returned.

## Permissions

Import, refresh and adoption of an empty policy require the tenant permission
`team_role_defaults.read`. Publishing configured sets, updates and destroy
require `team_role_defaults.update`; normal management needs both permissions.
Both permissions support service accounts with explicit native assignments.
The policy endpoint requires neither `roles.read` nor role-assignment grants.
Examples that resolve role keys through `onpager_rbac_role` data sources also
require `roles.read` for those separate reads.
